en.title: OAuth 2.1 draft: §1.5 requires https for all client URLs and leaves out the private-use redirect URIs that §8.4.3 describes
en.summary: §1.5 says all OAuth protocol URLs, including those of the client, must use https, with one exception for loopback redirect URIs. §8.4.3 describes private-use URI scheme redirect URIs of native apps such as com.example.app:/oauth2redirect/example-provider, and §2.3.1 tells the server how to check them. The -05 entry of the document history mentions an exception for a custom URL scheme that the current text lacks.
en.impact: Read literally, a native app that registers a private-use scheme redirect URI, as §8.4.3 describes, breaks the MUST of §1.5.
en.correction: Add private-use URI scheme redirect URIs of native apps to the exception in §1.5, or state the rule as RFC 9700 Section 2.6 does.

quotes.source: The OAuth 2.1 Authorization Framework, draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-17 (IETF, 31 October 2026)
quotes.text: All OAuth protocol URLs (URLs exposed by the AS, RS, and client) MUST use the https scheme except for loopback interface redirect URIs, which MAY use the http scheme.
